note.fact: The balanced formulas B(u⊗c)=[u]⊗c and B⁻¹([u]⊗c)=u⊗c extend to linear maps on the indicated tensors.
note.justification: Use the same checked tensor universal property. On the forward map the base is R and the target action factors through R/pR=ℱ_p, so [ru]⊗c=[u]⊗ρ(r)c. For the reverse map choose a representative u; changing u by pw changes u⊗c by w⊗pc=0. Lifting a prime-field scalar to r gives exactly the R-balancing equation displayed in S002; changing this lift by pR also gives zero. Additivity and K-linearity follow from those same formulas. The packet's simple-tensor inverse computations, with extensionality BG006, prove the isomorphism. No quotient-tensor isomorphism is being assumed.

grounds.reason: ρ and the prime-field embedding into K are established.
ker ρ=pR, its prime-field image, lift independence and scalar balancing are explicitly proved before asserting the inverse.

8: public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Quotient.Basic
9: public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Tower
10: public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Maps
11: public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Quotient.Defs

13: /-!
14: 
15: # Interaction between Quotients and Tensor Products
16: 
17: This file contains constructions that relate quotients and tensor products. This file is also a home
18: for results whose proof depends on both tensor products and linear algebraic quotients.
19: Let `M, N` be `R`-modules, `m ≤ M` and `n ≤ N` be an `R`-submodules and `I ≤ R` an ideal. We prove
20: the following isomorphisms:
21: 
22: ## Main results
23: - `TensorProduct.quotientTensorQuotientEquiv`:
24:   `(M ⧸ m) ⊗[R] (N ⧸ n) ≃ₗ[R] (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸ (m ⊗ N ⊔ M ⊗ n)`
25: - `TensorProduct.quotientTensorEquiv`:
26:   `(M ⧸ m) ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸ (m ⊗ N)`
27: - `TensorProduct.tensorQuotientEquiv`:
28:   `M ⊗[R] (N ⧸ n) ≃ₗ[R] (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸ (M ⊗ n)`
29: - `TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul`:
30:   `(R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[R] M ⧸ (I • M)`
31: - `TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul`:
32:   `M ⊗[R] (R ⧸ I) ≃ₗ[R] M ⧸ (I • M)`
33: 
34: ## Tags
35: 
36: Quotient, Tensor Product
37: 
38: -/
39: 
40: @[expose] public section
41: 
42: assert_not_exists Cardinal
43: 
44: namespace TensorProduct
45: 
46: variable {R M N : Type*} [CommRing R]
47: variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
48: 
49: attribute [local ext high] ext LinearMap.prod_ext
50: 
51: /--
52: Let `M, N` be `R`-modules, `m ≤ M` and `n ≤ N` be an `R`-submodules. Then we have a linear
53: isomorphism between tensor products of the quotients and the quotient of the tensor product:
54: `(M ⧸ m) ⊗[R] (N ⧸ n) ≃ₗ[R] (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸ (m ⊗ N ⊔ M ⊗ n)`.
55: -/
56: noncomputable def quotientTensorQuotientEquiv (m : Submodule R M) (n : Submodule R N) :
57:     (M ⧸ (m : Submodule R M)) ⊗[R] (N ⧸ (n : Submodule R N)) ≃ₗ[R]
58:     (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸
59:       (LinearMap.range (map m.subtype LinearMap.id) ⊔
60:         LinearMap.range (map LinearMap.id n.subtype)) :=
61:   LinearEquiv.ofLinear
62:     (lift <| Submodule.liftQ _ (LinearMap.flip <| Submodule.liftQ _
63:       ((mk R (M := M) (N := N)).flip.compr₂ (Submodule.mkQ _)) fun x hx => by
64:       ext y
65:       simp only [LinearMap.compr₂_apply, LinearMap.flip_apply, mk_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply,
66:         LinearMap.zero_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
67:       exact Submodule.mem_sup_right ⟨y ⊗ₜ ⟨x, hx⟩, rfl⟩) fun x hx => by
68:       ext y
69:       simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply, LinearMap.flip_apply,
70:         Submodule.liftQ_apply, LinearMap.compr₂_apply, mk_apply, LinearMap.zero_comp,
71:         LinearMap.zero_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
72:       exact Submodule.mem_sup_left ⟨⟨x, hx⟩ ⊗ₜ y, rfl⟩)
73:     (Submodule.liftQ _ (map (Submodule.mkQ _) (Submodule.mkQ _)) fun x hx => by
74:       rw [Submodule.mem_sup] at hx
75:       rcases hx with ⟨_, ⟨a, rfl⟩, _, ⟨b, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
76:       simp only [LinearMap.mem_ker, map_add]
77:       set f := (map m.mkQ n.mkQ) ∘ₗ (map m.subtype LinearMap.id)
78:       set g := (map m.mkQ n.mkQ) ∘ₗ (map LinearMap.id n.subtype)
79:       have eq : LinearMap.coprod f g = 0 := by
80:         ext x y
81:         · simp [f, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero _ |>.2 x.2]
82:         · simp [g, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero _ |>.2 y.2]
83:       exact congr($eq (a, b)))
84:     (by ext; simp) (by ext; simp)
85: 
86: @[simp]
87: lemma quotientTensorQuotientEquiv_apply_tmul_mk_tmul_mk
88:     (m : Submodule R M) (n : Submodule R N) (x : M) (y : N) :
89:     quotientTensorQuotientEquiv m n
90:       (Submodule.Quotient.mk x ⊗ₜ[R] Submodule.Quotient.mk y) =
91:       Submodule.Quotient.mk (x ⊗ₜ y) := rfl
92: 
93: @[simp]
94: lemma quotientTensorQuotientEquiv_symm_apply_mk_tmul
95:     (m : Submodule R M) (n : Submodule R N) (x : M) (y : N) :
96:     (quotientTensorQuotientEquiv m n).symm (Submodule.Quotient.mk (x ⊗ₜ y)) =
97:       Submodule.Quotient.mk x ⊗ₜ[R] Submodule.Quotient.mk y := rfl
98: 
99: variable (N) in
100: /--
101: Let `M, N` be `R`-modules, `m ≤ M` be an `R`-submodule. Then we have a linear isomorphism between
102: tensor products of the quotient and the quotient of the tensor product:
103: `(M ⧸ m) ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸ (m ⊗ N)`.
104: -/
105: noncomputable def quotientTensorEquiv (m : Submodule R M) :
106:     (M ⧸ (m : Submodule R M)) ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R]
107:     (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸ (LinearMap.range (map m.subtype (LinearMap.id : N →ₗ[R] N))) :=
108:   congr (LinearEquiv.refl _ _) ((Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot _ rfl).symm) ≪≫ₗ
109:   quotientTensorQuotientEquiv (N := N) m ⊥ ≪≫ₗ
110:   Submodule.Quotient.equiv _ _ (LinearEquiv.refl _ _) (by
111:     simp [Submodule.map_span, range_map_eq_span_tmul])
112: 
113: @[simp]
114: lemma quotientTensorEquiv_apply_tmul_mk (m : Submodule R M) (x : M) (y : N) :
115:     quotientTensorEquiv N m (Submodule.Quotient.mk x ⊗ₜ[R] y) =
116:     Submodule.Quotient.mk (x ⊗ₜ y) :=
117:   rfl
118: 
119: @[simp]
120: lemma quotientTensorEquiv_symm_apply_mk_tmul (m : Submodule R M) (x : M) (y : N) :
121:     (quotientTensorEquiv N m).symm (Submodule.Quotient.mk (x ⊗ₜ y)) =
122:     Submodule.Quotient.mk x ⊗ₜ[R] y :=
123:   rfl
124: 
125: variable (M) in
126: /--
127: Let `M, N` be `R`-modules, `n ≤ N` be an `R`-submodule. Then we have a linear isomorphism between
128: tensor products of the quotient and the quotient of the tensor product:
129: `M ⊗[R] (N ⧸ n) ≃ₗ[R] (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸ (M ⊗ n)`.
130: -/
131: noncomputable def tensorQuotientEquiv (n : Submodule R N) :
132:     M ⊗[R] (N ⧸ (n : Submodule R N)) ≃ₗ[R]
133:     (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸ (LinearMap.range (map (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[R] M) n.subtype)) :=
134:   congr ((Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot _ rfl).symm) (LinearEquiv.refl _ _) ≪≫ₗ
135:   quotientTensorQuotientEquiv (⊥ : Submodule R M) n ≪≫ₗ
136:   Submodule.Quotient.equiv _ _ (LinearEquiv.refl _ _) (by simp [range_map_eq_span_tmul])
137: 
138: @[simp]
139: lemma tensorQuotientEquiv_apply_mk_tmul (n : Submodule R N) (x : M) (y : N) :
140:     tensorQuotientEquiv M n (x ⊗ₜ[R] Submodule.Quotient.mk y) =
141:     Submodule.Quotient.mk (x ⊗ₜ y) :=
142:   rfl
143: 
144: @[simp]
145: lemma tensorQuotientEquiv_symm_apply_tmul_mk (n : Submodule R N) (x : M) (y : N) :
146:     (tensorQuotientEquiv M n).symm (Submodule.Quotient.mk (x ⊗ₜ y)) =
147:     x ⊗ₜ[R] Submodule.Quotient.mk y :=
148:   rfl
149: 
150: variable (M) in
151: /-- Left tensoring a module with a quotient of the ring is the same as
152: quotienting that module by the corresponding submodule. -/
153: noncomputable def quotTensorEquivQuotSMul (I : Ideal R) :
154:     ((R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M) ≃ₗ[R] M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) :=
155:   quotientTensorEquiv M I ≪≫ₗ
156:   (Submodule.Quotient.equiv _ _ (TensorProduct.lid R M) <| by
157:     rw [← LinearMap.range_comp, ← (Submodule.topEquiv.lTensor I).range_comp, Submodule.smul_eq_map₂,
158:       map₂_eq_range_lift_comp_mapIncl]
159:     exact congr_arg _ (TensorProduct.ext' fun _ _ ↦ by simp))
160: 
161: variable (M) in
162: /-- Right tensoring a module with a quotient of the ring is the same as
163: quotienting that module by the corresponding submodule. -/
164: noncomputable def tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul (I : Ideal R) :
165:     (M ⊗[R] (R ⧸ I)) ≃ₗ[R] M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) :=
166:   TensorProduct.comm _ _ _ ≪≫ₗ quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I
167: 
168: @[simp]
169: lemma quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_mk_tmul (I : Ideal R) (r : R) (x : M) :
170:     quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I (Ideal.Quotient.mk I r ⊗ₜ[R] x) =
171:       Submodule.Quotient.mk (r • x) :=
172:   (quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I).eq_symm_apply.mp <|
173:     Eq.trans (congrArg (· ⊗ₜ[R] x) <|
174:         Eq.trans (congrArg (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)
175:                     (Eq.trans (smul_eq_mul ..) (mul_one r))).symm <|
176:           Submodule.Quotient.mk_smul I r 1) <|
177:       smul_tmul r _ x
178: 
179: @[simp]
180: lemma quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_mk_one_tmul (I : Ideal R) (x : M) :
181:     quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I (1 ⊗ₜ x) = Submodule.Quotient.mk x := by
182:   rw [← RingHom.map_one (Ideal.Quotient.mk I), TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_mk_tmul]
183:   simp
184: 
185: lemma quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_comp_mkQ_rTensor (I : Ideal R) :
186:     quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I ∘ₗ I.mkQ.rTensor M =
187:       (I • ⊤ : Submodule R M).mkQ ∘ₗ TensorProduct.lid R M :=
188:   TensorProduct.ext' (quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_mk_tmul I)
189: 
190: @[simp]
191: lemma quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_symm_mk (I : Ideal R) (x : M) :
192:     (quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I).symm (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] x :=
193:   rfl
194: 
195: lemma quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_symm_comp_mkQ (I : Ideal R) :
196:     (quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I).symm ∘ₗ (I • ⊤ : Submodule R M).mkQ =
197:       TensorProduct.mk R (R ⧸ I) M 1 :=
198:   LinearMap.ext (quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_symm_mk I)
199: 
200: lemma quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_comp_mk (I : Ideal R) :

311: /-- If M and N are both R- and A-modules and their actions on them commute,
312: and if the A-action on `M ⊗[R] N` can switch between the two factors, then there is a
313: canonical S-linear map from `M ⊗[A] N` to `M ⊗[R] N`,
314: where `S` is any other ring acting on `M` and whose action commutes with the `A` and `R`-actions. -/
315: def mapOfCompatibleSMul : M ⊗[A] N →ₗ[S] M ⊗[R] N where
316:   __ :=
317:     lift (σ₁₂ := RingHom.id A)
318:     { toFun := fun m ↦
319:       { __ := mk R M N m
320:         map_smul' := fun _ _ ↦ (smul_tmul _ _ _).symm }
321:       map_add' := fun _ _ ↦ LinearMap.ext <| by simp
322:       map_smul' := fun _ _ ↦ rfl }
323:   map_smul' s x := by
324:     induction x with
325:     | zero => simp
326:     | add x y _ _ => simp_all
327:     | tmul x y => simp [smul_tmul']

335:   fun x ↦ x.induction_on (⟨0, map_zero _⟩) (fun m n ↦ ⟨_, mapOfCompatibleSMul_tmul ..⟩)
336:     fun _ _ ⟨x, hx⟩ ⟨y, hy⟩ ↦ ⟨x + y, by simpa using congr($hx + $hy)⟩

arguments.statement: ∃ res : (LR.R p ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : LR.R p)}) ≃+* ZMod p, ∀ a b : ℤ, ∀ r : LR.R p, (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ)/(b : ℚ) → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b → res (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ r) = (a : ZMod p) * (b : ZMod p)⁻¹
arguments.proof:
classical
letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨h_H001⟩
letI : CharP K p := h_H002
obtain ⟨fc⟩ := h_T017
letI := fc.ak
let I : Ideal (LR.R p) := Ideal.span {(p : LR.R p)}
have hI : I ≤ RingHom.ker (algebraMap (LR.R p) K) := by
  rw [Ideal.span_le]
  intro a ha
  rcases Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp ha with rfl
  simp [RingHom.mem_ker, CharP.cast_eq_zero K p]
let g : (LR.R p ⧸ I) →+* K := Ideal.Quotient.lift I (algebraMap (LR.R p) K) hI
letI : Nontrivial (LR.R p ⧸ I) := g.domain_nontrivial
have hp0 : (p : LR.R p ⧸ I) = 0 := by
  rw [← map_natCast (Ideal.Quotient.mk I), Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem]
  exact Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton _)
letI : CharP (LR.R p ⧸ I) p := (CharP.charP_iff_prime_eq_zero h_H001).mpr hp0
let f : ZMod p →+* (LR.R p ⧸ I) := ZMod.castHom (dvd_refl p) _
have frac : ∀ a b : ℤ, ∀ r : LR.R p, (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ)/(b : ℚ) → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b → Ideal.Quotient.mk I r = f ((a : ZMod p) * (b : ZMod p)⁻¹) := by
  intro a b r hr hb
  have hb0 : b ≠ 0 := by intro he; apply hb; simp [he]
  have he : (b : LR.R p) * r = a := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    change (b : ℚ) * (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ)
    rw [hr]
    field_simp
  have hbz : (b : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := by simpa [CharP.intCast_eq_zero_iff] using hb
  have he' := congrArg (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) he
  have hu : f (b : ZMod p) * f ((b : ZMod p)⁻¹) = 1 := by rw [← map_mul, mul_inv_cancel₀ hbz, map_one]
  have hfint (z : ℤ) : f (z : ZMod p) = (z : LR.R p ⧸ I) := map_intCast f z
  simp only [map_mul, map_intCast] at he'
  rw [map_mul]
  calc
    Ideal.Quotient.mk I r = (f (b : ZMod p) * f ((b : ZMod p)⁻¹)) * Ideal.Quotient.mk I r := by rw [hu, one_mul]
    _ = f (a : ZMod p) * f ((b : ZMod p)⁻¹) := by rw [mul_right_comm, hfint, he', hfint]
have hsurj : Function.Surjective f := by
  intro q
  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective q
  obtain ⟨a,b,hb,hpb,hr⟩ := (h_T005 r).mp r.property
  exact ⟨_, (frac a b r hr hpb).symm⟩
let e := RingEquiv.ofBijective f ⟨f.injective, hsurj⟩
refine ⟨e.symm, ?_⟩
intro a b r hr hb
apply e.injective
simpa [e] using (frac a b r hr hb).symm

22: /-- The `ZMod n`-module structure on commutative monoids whose elements have order dividing `n ≠ 0`.
23: Also implies a group structure via `Module.addCommMonoidToAddCommGroup`.
24: See note [reducible non-instances]. -/
25: abbrev AddCommMonoid.zmodModule [NeZero n] [AddCommMonoid M] (h : ∀ (x : M), n • x = 0) :
26:     Module (ZMod n) M := by
27:   have h_mod (c : ℕ) (x : M) : (c % n) • x = c • x := by
28:     suffices (c % n + c / n * n) • x = c • x by rwa [add_nsmul, mul_nsmul, h, add_zero] at this
29:     rw [Nat.mod_add_div']
30:   have := NeZero.ne n
31:   match n with
32:   | n + 1 => exact {
33:     smul := fun (c : Fin _) x ↦ c.val • x
34:     smul_zero := fun _ ↦ nsmul_zero _
35:     zero_smul := fun _ ↦ zero_nsmul _
36:     smul_add := fun _ _ _ ↦ nsmul_add _ _ _
37:     one_smul := fun _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| one_nsmul _
38:     add_smul := fun _ _ _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| add_nsmul _ _ _
39:     mul_smul := fun _ _ _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| mul_nsmul' _ _ _

45:     Module (ZMod n) G :=
46:   match n with

letI := fc.ak

  simp only [LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, d, LinearMap.smul_apply, LinearMap.id_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply]
  rw [← TensorProduct.smul_tmul]
  simp [Algebra.smul_def]
have hex : Function.Exact d q := by
  rw [LinearMap.exact_iff]
  exact Submodule.ker_mkQ _
have hk : LinearMap.ker (q.lTensor K) = ⊥ := by
  rw [(LinearMap.lTensor_exact K hex (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)).linearMap_ker_eq, hd, LinearMap.range_zero]
have hinj : Function.Injective F := by
  change Function.Injective (q.lTensor K)
  exact LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mp hk
have hsur : Function.Surjective F := by
  change Function.Surjective (q.lTensor K)
  exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective K (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
exact ⟨LinearEquiv.ofBijective F ⟨hinj, hsur⟩, fun c u => rfl⟩
